1. (S) SITUATION:
The Greenland-Iceland-United Kingdom Gap is NATO's most fortified anti-submarine chokepoint. SOSUS arrays, P-3 Orion patrol aircraft, and British surface units are positioned to prevent {TaskForceName} from reaching the North Atlantic.
2. (S) MISSION: 2.1 Bring the task force through the GIUK patrol zone. 2.2 {FlagshipName} must survive.
3. (S) EXECUTION: 3.1 Send submarines ahead to investigate contacts and disrupt NATO surveillance. 3.2 Keep the surface group outside unnecessary engagement ranges while crossing the gap. 3.3 Use air defenses to deny P-3 Orion attacks and preserve the task force's freedom of maneuver. 3.4 Continue west until the marked patrol zone has been cleared.
4. (S) ENEMY SITUATION: 4.1 NATO SOSUS arrays are expected to provide early warning throughout the passage. 4.2 British frigates and American submarines are pre-positioned near the gap. 4.3 Maritime patrol aircraft will reinforce the surface and subsurface screen.
5. (S) FRIENDLY SITUATION: 5.1 {TaskForceName} is supported by its assigned submarines and organic air defense systems. 5.2 The task force must preserve enough combat power for operations in the North Atlantic.
6. (S) INTEL ASSESSMENT: 6.1 NATO will treat this transit as the decisive opportunity to contain the Northern Fleet. 6.2 Expect persistent contact reports and coordinated attacks near the center of the gap. Do not allow the formation to lose momentum.
